note: Sources for the bamboo records rebuilt in 0.9.127 (audit D08). The one record before named no species ('Fargesia / Phyllostachys selections') and its choices were 'Clumping bamboo', 'Golden groove' and 'Black bamboo'. `estimates` names every field that is a planning value rather than a published figure, and why. NC State returned 404 for Phyllostachys nigra, Fargesia murielae and Fargesia rufa. Green Panda bamboo and river cane were added in 0.9.128.

migration.bamboo|: bamboo| (now Phyllostachys aureosulcata): the old base drew a green 25 ft grove, which is this species
migration.bamboo|golden: bamboo|golden (now 'Spectabilis'): MBG lists 'golden groove bamboo' as a common name of the species, but the old choice drew yellow canes, which is 'Spectabilis' (yellow culm, green groove). Kept on its key so saved gardens keep the picture they show
migration.bamboo|clumping: umbrellabamboo| (PLANT_REF_ALIASES): the old choice was 12 x 6 ft, 'Fargesia-style', which is the classic clumping Fargesia

mbg.says: Zone 4 to 9; height 12-18 ft; spread 12-25 ft; full sun, tolerates some light shade; medium water; native to northeastern China. Culms to 25-30 ft, but 12-18 ft in USDA zones 5-6. A running bamboo that naturalizes into dense colonies; root barriers advised. Flagged 'Midwest Noxious Weed: Do Not Plant'; listed as a noxious weed in one or more Midwestern states outside Missouri. Common names include golden groove bamboo.

ncstate.says: Height 12-18 ft, width 12-25 ft; zones 4a-10a; 'a running type of bamboo with very invasive tendencies... an invasive species and should not be planted'.

bambooGarden.says: Height 30 ft max, 25 ft average (Portland, OR); hardy to -10F; USDA zones 5-10; one of the hardiest bamboos; about one cane in ten zig-zags at the base; cultivars 'Spectabilis', 'Aureocaulis', 'Harbin Inversa'.

sources.wikipedia: Phyllostachys aureosulcata: native to Zhejiang Province, China.

estimates.heightIn: 216 (18 ft): the top of MBG's and NC State's 12-18 ft, which both give for colder zones; it runs to 25-30 ft where winters are mild
estimates.spread: 120 (10 ft): a planted clump, not a colony. MBG and NC State's 12-25 ft is how far a stand runs, which a running bamboo has no end to; sized to the colony it drew squat
estimates.space: 36: unchanged from the old record, no source
estimates.grow: 5: RHS gives 5-10 years to mature size for both bamboos it lists

bambooGarden.says: Colours reversed from the species: bright yellow culms with a green sulcus; new culms flush red in sun. Height 30 ft max, 25 ft average; -10F; zones 5-10.

estimates.size: the species' figures; no source gives a different size

rhs.says: Max height 2.5-4 m, max spread 2.5-4 m, 5-10 years to maturity; full sun or partial shade; moist but well-drained; sheltered; H5.

bambooGarden.says: Height 40 ft max, 20-25 ft average; hardy to 5F; USDA zones 7-10. Usually 25-30 ft in Portland gardens. New culms emerge green and turn black in one to three years. Currently unavailable after gregarious flowering.

sources.wikipedia: Phyllostachys nigra: native to Hunan Province, China; up to 10 m.

estimates.spread: 120 (10 ft): the top of the RHS's 2.5-4 m; a planted clump, as for yellow groove
estimates.zones: [7,10]: Bamboo Garden and most nurseries; some report it surviving zone 6 with damage
estimates.sun: part: the RHS gives full sun or partial shade

rhs.says: Max height 2.5-4 m, max spread 1-1.5 m, 5-10 years to maturity; full sun or partial shade; sheltered.

bambooGarden.says: Height 14 ft max, 10-12 ft average; 0.5 in canes; hardy to -20F; USDA zones 5-9. Not recommended for climates with intense heat or high summer humidity, including most of the southern USA. Shade-loving; leaves yellow or burn in too much summer sun. Introduced by E. H. Wilson in 1910.

sources.wikipedia: Fargesia murielae: a large, clump-forming evergreen bamboo with yellow canes, close to F. nitida.

estimates.heightIn: 144 (12 ft): the top of Bamboo Garden's 10-12 ft average; the old 'Clumping bamboo' was also 12 ft
estimates.spread: 60 (5 ft): the top of the RHS's 1-1.5 m
estimates.sun: part: Bamboo Garden calls it shade-loving; the RHS allows full sun in Britain

greenpandabamboo.naming: One tissue-cultured clone, sold as Green Panda. The RHS lists it as Fargesia dracocephala Green Panda ('Rufus') with 'Fargesia rufa misapplied' as a synonym; NVK as Fargesia dracocephala 'Rufa'; Bamboo Garden as Fargesia sp. 'Rufa', selected by Jan Oprins in Belgium; MBG as Fargesia rufa; NC State as Fargesia rufa 'Green Panda'. The record follows the RHS and NVK species with the 'Rufa' epithet Bamboo Garden and NVK use. The true Fargesia rufa is a larger plant (RHS 137830: 2.5-4 m).

mbg.says: As Fargesia rufa: zone 5 to 8; height 6-10 ft; spread 6-10 ft (6-8 ft wide in the notes); part shade; medium water; tolerates deer and drought. Prefers cool summers, needs protection from hot afternoon sun, does not perform well in the hot, humid summers of the southeastern US. Does not run; not invasive. Bluish-green new culms with rusty red sheaths, bright green mature culms 1/2 in across. Native to the mountains of western Sichuan.

ncstate.says: 'Green Panda', introduced 1995: 6-10 ft tall and wide; zones 5a-8b; vase-shaped with arching stems; evergreen, deer-resistant; part shade, tolerates full sun; reddish-brown culm sheaths.

rhs.says: Max height 1.5-2.5 m, max spread 1-1.5 m, 5-10 years; full sun or partial shade; H6.

bambooGarden.says: Height 10 ft max, 6-7 ft average; 0.5 in canes; hardy to -15F; zones 5-9, not for intense heat or humid summers including most of the southern USA; shade-loving outside the Pacific Northwest.

estimates.heightIn: 96 (8 ft): the middle of MBG's and NC State's 6-10 ft; Bamboo Garden's average is 6-7 ft
estimates.spread: 72 (6 ft): the low end of MBG's and NC State's width, above the RHS's 1-1.5 m. A clumping bamboo, so this is the real clump
estimates.zones: [5,8]: MBG and NC State; Bamboo Garden gives 5-9
estimates.roles: deerOk: MBG (tolerates deer) and NC State (deer-resistant)

rivercane.common: river cane, giant cane, giant river cane, canebrake bamboo

mbg.says: Zone 5 to 9; height 5-12 ft, to 25 ft in zones 8-9; spread 8-20 ft; full sun, tolerates light shade; consistently moist soil; native to river banks, bottomlands, swamps and bogs of the southeastern US. A rhizomatous running bamboo forming canebrakes; barriers or a sunk pot where naturalizing is not wanted. Leaves to 12 in long and 1.5 in wide, evergreen in warm areas, killed below 0F further north, the canes leafing out again in spring.

ncstate.says: Height 4-25 ft, usually 8-20 ft; width 8-20 ft; zones 5a-9b; full sun to deep shade, best in partial to full sun; moist, well-drained, occasionally wet; tolerates brief inundation but will not thrive in wet areas.

wildflowerCenter.says: Up to about 25 ft; evergreen; part shade; wet soils. Native from southern New Jersey to southern Illinois, south to northern Florida and east Texas. River banks, damp woods, bogs. Relied on by Swainson's warbler, Bachman's warbler and others; used for basketry by southeastern Indigenous peoples.

bambooGarden.says: Height 25 ft max, 15-20 ft average; 1 in canes; hardy to -10F; zones 6-10; with its form 'Tecta' the only bamboos native to the United States.

sources.wikipedia: Arundinaria gigantea: giant cane, river cane; endemic to the south-central and southeastern US, west to Oklahoma and Texas, north to New York.

estimates.spread: 96 (8 ft): a planted clump, the low end of MBG's and NC State's 8-20 ft, which is how far a stand runs
estimates.zones: [5,9]: MBG and NC State; Bamboo Garden gives 6-10
estimates.sun: part: the Wildflower Center gives part shade, NC State full sun to deep shade
